name: Abu al-Ala' al-Ma'arri
bio: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah was born into a family of scholars in Ma'arrat al-Nu'man in 363 AH (973 CE) and lost his sight to smallpox in childhood. He travelled to Baghdad in 398 AH, then returned home, where he dictated his books to a scribe. After his early collection Saqt al-Zand, he wrote the Luzumiyyat, binding himself to repeat sounds before the rhyme letter that other poets were free to vary. He died in Ma'arrat al-Nu'man in 449 AH (1057 CE).
